title: Human circulatory system
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Science and Technology; not yet checked by a CBC Science and Technology teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: The child finds the pulse at the wrist and counts it at rest and after skipping for a minute. A model heart from a picture or a sheep's heart from the butcher (handled by the teacher) shows the four chambers. Medical statements are to be confirmed by a teacher or a health worker.

skills.key_step: The child names the three parts of the circulatory system (heart, blood vessels, blood) and keeps the lungs and stomach in their own systems.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the parts of the breathing system.
floor.question: Which organ takes in oxygen?

representations: a body outline with the heart and vessels drawn in red and blue
the pulse at the wrist
a table: system and its parts
steps: Heart: the pump.
Blood vessels: the tubes (arteries, veins, capillaries).
Blood: what is pumped.
Lungs and stomach belong to other systems.
contexts: a pulse taken at a clinic

board.do: Draw a heart with tubes going out and back.
Point at the tubes.
Wait for "blood vessels".
Write "heart, blood vessels, blood".

listen_for: the lungs are part of it
misconceptions.ask: Which system do the lungs belong to?
misconceptions.repair: The lungs are in the breathing system.

misconceptions.ask: Does the heart make blood or pump it?
misconceptions.repair: The heart pumps blood; it does not make or store it.

misconceptions.ask: What flows inside a blood vessel?
misconceptions.repair: Blood vessels are tubes that carry blood.

misconceptions.ask: What does the heart pump, and through what?
misconceptions.repair: The system is the heart, the vessels and the blood.

checks.question: Name the three parts of the circulatory system.
What is the job of the heart?
checks.answer: to pump blood round the body

skills.key_step: The child describes the heart as a muscle in the chest between the lungs with four chambers (two upper atria receive blood, two lower ventricles pump it out) and valves that keep blood flowing one way.

floor.prerequisite: Can name the parts of the circulatory system.
floor.question: What pumps the blood?

representations: a fist held to the chest
a drawing of the four chambers
a sheep's heart (teacher)
steps: Place it: chest, between the lungs, a little to the left.
Four chambers: two atria on top, two ventricles below.
Ventricles have thick walls and pump.
Valves stop blood flowing back.
contexts: a doctor listening with a stethoscope

board.do: Draw a heart split into four rooms.
Point at the lower rooms.
Wait for "they pump the blood out".
Label atria and ventricles.

listen_for: the heart is in the stomach
misconceptions.ask: Where do you feel your heart beat?
misconceptions.repair: The heart is in the chest between the lungs.

misconceptions.ask: Which walls are thickest?
misconceptions.repair: The lower chambers (ventricles) pump hardest.

misconceptions.ask: How many chambers did the sheep heart have?
misconceptions.repair: The heart has four chambers.

listen_for: it is shaped like a love heart
misconceptions.ask: Make a fist: is that about the size and shape?
misconceptions.repair: The heart is a fist-sized muscle in the chest.

checks.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
Which chambers pump blood out of the heart?

skills.key_step: The child says arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins carry it back to the heart, and capillaries are tiny vessels where food and oxygen pass to the body; blood goes round and round.

floor.question: Where does the heart pump blood to?

representations: a loop drawn: heart, arteries, capillaries, veins, heart
veins seen on the back of the hand
a chart: vessel, direction, job
steps: Arteries: Away from the heart (A for away).
Capillaries: tiny, among the cells, where food and oxygen pass out.
Veins: back to the heart.
Round and round: a circulation.

board.do: Draw a circle: heart at the top.
Write "arteries" on the side leaving the heart.
Ask what the vessels coming back are called.
Wait for "veins".
Write "capillaries" at the bottom of the loop.

misconceptions.ask: A for arteries: away or back?
misconceptions.repair: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins bring it back.

listen_for: the blood stays in the body
misconceptions.ask: Where does the blood go after the capillaries?
misconceptions.repair: Blood goes round and back to the heart.

misconceptions.ask: Where are capillaries found?
misconceptions.repair: Capillaries are the tiniest vessels.

misconceptions.ask: What colour is blood taken from a vein at the clinic?
misconceptions.repair: All blood is red.

checks.question: Which vessels carry blood away from the heart?
Where do food and oxygen pass from the blood into the body?

skills.key_step: The child gives the parts of blood and their jobs: red cells carry oxygen, white cells fight germs, platelets help blood clot, plasma carries food, waste and the cells.

floor.question: Which vessels carry blood back to the heart?

representations: a picture of blood under a microscope
a cut that forms a scab
a chart: part, job
steps: Red cells: oxygen.
White cells: fight germs.
Platelets: clot the blood at a cut.
Plasma: the liquid that carries food, waste and the cells.
contexts: a scab forming on a knee

board.do: Draw a cut with a scab forming.
Point at the scab.
board.say: Which part of the blood made this?

board.do: Wait for "platelets".
Write the job of each part.

misconceptions.ask: Which cells give blood its red colour?
misconceptions.repair: Red cells carry oxygen; white cells fight germs.

misconceptions.ask: What stops a cut bleeding?
misconceptions.repair: Platelets help blood clot.

misconceptions.ask: What fights germs in the blood?
misconceptions.repair: Blood has red cells, white cells, platelets and plasma.

misconceptions.ask: Where does digested food go after the small intestine?
misconceptions.repair: Plasma carries digested food and waste.

checks.question: Which part of the blood fights germs?
What is the job of platelets?
checks.answer: to help blood clot at a cut

skills.key_step: The child recognises common circulatory conditions and their signs (high blood pressure, heart attack, hardening of arteries, anaemia) and says they are not caught from other people.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the jobs of the heart and vessels.
floor.question: What do arteries do?
floor.answer: carry blood away from the heart

representations: a blood-pressure cuff at a clinic (picture)
a pipe narrowed with clay as a model artery
a chart: condition, signs, cause
steps: High blood pressure: blood pushes hard on the vessels; often no signs; checked at a clinic.
Hardened, narrowed arteries: fat builds up inside.
Heart attack warning signs: chest pain, arm pain, sweating.
Anaemia: too few red cells; tiredness and pale skin.
contexts: a health day at the school

board.do: Draw an artery as a clear pipe, then one with a fat build-up inside.
Ask what happens to blood flow in the narrowed pipe.
Wait for the child's prediction.
Write "harder to pump, blood pressure rises".

listen_for: you can catch high blood pressure
misconceptions.ask: Do germs cause high blood pressure?
misconceptions.repair: These conditions are not caught from others.

misconceptions.ask: What builds up inside the artery?
misconceptions.repair: Arteries harden and narrow when fat builds up.

misconceptions.ask: What does the cuff measure: amount or push?
misconceptions.repair: Blood pressure is how hard blood pushes on the vessel walls.

misconceptions.ask: What are the warning signs?
misconceptions.repair: Chest pain, arm pain and sweating: get help at once.

checks.question: Give one sign of a heart attack.
checks.answer: chest pain, pain in the left arm, sweating or breathlessness

checks.question: Can high blood pressure be caught from another person?

skills.key_step: The child says how to prevent circulatory conditions: regular exercise, less salt, sugar and fat, eat vegetables and fruit, no smoking or alcohol, manage stress, and checks at a clinic, for people of all ages.

floor.question: What is high blood pressure?
floor.answer: blood pushing too hard on the vessel walls

representations: a plate of salty fried food and a balanced plate
a pulse count after skipping
a chart: habit, why it helps
steps: Move every day: the heart is a muscle.
Less salt, sugar and oil.
No smoking or alcohol.
Rest, sleep and manage stress; check blood pressure.

board.do: Draw two plates: chips with lots of salt, and githeri with sukuma.
Point at the chips.
board.say: What does a lot of salt do to blood pressure?

board.do: Wait for "it raises it".
Ask the child to circle the heart-healthy plate.

misconceptions.ask: What happens to a muscle that is never used?
misconceptions.repair: Exercise keeps the heart strong.

misconceptions.ask: When do habits that harm the heart start?
misconceptions.repair: Heart care starts young.

misconceptions.ask: What does too much salt do to blood pressure?
misconceptions.repair: Too much salt, oil and sugar harms the heart.

misconceptions.ask: Do salt and smoking harm thin people too?
misconceptions.repair: Anyone can get high blood pressure.

checks.question: Give two ways to keep the heart healthy.
checks.answer: any two: exercise, less salt, sugar and fat, no smoking, fruit and vegetables

checks.question: Why should a young person avoid smoking?
checks.answer: it damages the heart and blood vessels

skills.key_step: The child picks the parts of a daily routine that keep the circulatory system healthy: daily exercise, balanced meals, water, enough sleep, no smoking, short breaks from sitting, and combines them.

floor.prerequisite: Knows ways to prevent heart conditions.
floor.question: Give one way to keep the heart healthy.

representations: a blank daily timetable
a sample routine with a gap
habit cards to place in the day
steps: Start the day with breakfast and water.
Move: walk, play, PE.
Balanced meals; water instead of soda.
Breaks from sitting and enough sleep.

board.do: Draw a day line from morning to night.
Write breakfast and school on it.
Point at the afternoon.
board.say: What would you add here for your heart?

board.do: Wait for "play or exercise".
Ask the child to fill in the evening.

misconceptions.ask: What should you drink most?
misconceptions.repair: Drink water every day.

misconceptions.ask: If you exercise but eat salty chips every day, is the heart safe?
misconceptions.repair: Combine several good habits.

listen_for: sitting all day is fine when young
misconceptions.ask: What happens to the heart with no movement?
misconceptions.repair: Long sitting and smoking harm the heart at any age.

misconceptions.ask: Which keeps the heart strong: once a month or every day?
misconceptions.repair: Some exercise every day is best.

checks.question: Give three things a healthy daily routine for the heart includes.
checks.answer: any three: exercise, balanced meals, water, sleep, breaks from sitting, no smoking

checks.question: Which is better: playing every day or one long game a month?
